text.arabic_uthmani: وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلَآ أَبْصَٰرُكُمْ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمْ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعْلَمُ كَثِيرًۭا مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes the prior exposure scene and scopes the following negated state
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens by carrying the previous testimony scene into the rebuke. The denial of concealment is therefore not a detached statement; it is part of the same forensic sequence in which the bodies have already been made to speak. The connector also lets the prior return-to-Allah statement become the platform for explaining why the accused had lived without guarding themselves from exposure.

topics.headline: rebuke resumes prior testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees non-concealment as the explanation of the already unfolding body-testimony scene, not as a new topic.
topics.reason: The prefixed connector stands before the negated state clause and the CRITICAL rows consistently tie it to the prior exposure and return scene.

words.gloss_range: negation over the past-continuous concealment posture
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates the whole past-state frame, not a single failed tactic. Because it governs the auxiliary-plus-imperfect sequence, the ayah first presents an absent posture of self-screening and only later explains the belief that made such guarding seem unnecessary. The opening question is therefore about a continuing way of living before it is about one moment of exposure.

topics.headline: negation targets a settled posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rebuke concerns an ongoing absence of concealment, not merely one failed attempt to hide.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the particle govern the past-continuous predicate, while the CRITICAL rows press its role at the start of the ayah's argument.

words.gloss_range: auxiliary past-state frame for a sustained second-person condition
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurrence, and state are present as aspectual background; the local use is auxiliary rather than an independent existence claim
words.prose: {{ar:كُنتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) turns the following concealment verb into a sustained past condition. The root field of being and state is narrowed here into auxiliary aspect: the accused were occupying a settled posture of not self-screening. Its second-person plural ending keeps the addressees of 41:21 in the rebuke, and the syntax delays the real cause until the later adversative turn. Within the surah, the same state-framing texture appears around durable moral and judgment postures (41:18; 41:20; 41:27), so this failed guardedness belongs to that judgment-state thread.

topics.headline: being-root as auxiliary state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the failure as a lived condition stretched over time while recognizing that this word functions as an auxiliary.
topics.reason: The local construction makes the verb auxiliary to the following imperfect, so the broad being field survives as state/aspect rather than as a separate existential predication.

topics.headline: address continues before cause is named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same accused group held in direct address while the ayah withholds the mental cause until the witness list has intervened.
topics.reason: The second-person plural form begins the prosecutorial register, and the later correction confirms that the cause is intentionally delayed.

topics.headline: state language in the judgment arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can place this state-frame inside the surah's nearby pattern of durable moral postures and judgment scenes.
topics.reason: The supplied CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references, and none conflict with the local auxiliary parse.

words.gloss_range: Form X self-screening or seeking cover, denied in relation to bodily testimony
words.root_gloss_range: covering, veiling, screening, shelter, and concealment are locally focused on attempted self-protective cover; other branches remain background
words.prose: {{ar:تَسْتَتِرُونَ}} ({{tr:tastatirūna}}) is not passive hiddenness. Its Form X shape makes the missing act a sought self-screen, and the covering root makes privacy feel like a barrier that should have protected the actor. Because the concealment verb comes before the witness clause, the listener first hears the missing screen and only afterward learns the exposure it would have faced. The ayah then overturns that image: the feared testimony comes from hearing, sights, and skins, so the created body itself becomes the evidentiary surface. The rare root profile and parallels to veiling or covering (17:45; 18:90) sharpen the reversal without making those passages control the local sense.

topics.headline: sought self-screening denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deliberate self-protective concealment as the absent posture, not mere failure to be hidden.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form X and the attachment data places this verb as the predicate of the negated state clause.

topics.headline: cover image fails inside the body
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the irony that the body imagined as a hiding place is the very surface from which evidence emerges.
topics.reason: The covering field is locally tied to the following testimony complement and to the prior created-body explanation.

topics.headline: rare covering vocabulary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this concealment vocabulary as marked and related to Quranic veil/cover scenes, while keeping the local focus on failed self-screening.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows with 17:45 and 18:90 support contrastive lexical background, but local Form X grammar selects the self-screening sense.

topics.headline: concealment named before witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first hears the missing screen and only afterward learns the specific testimony that would have required it.
topics.reason: The verb precedes the complement clause, and the consonant-texture row reinforces the local screening image without changing the grammar.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle that makes testimony the complement or feared outcome of concealment
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) pulls the witness event under the concealment verb. The construction can carry the pressure of "that," "lest," or an underlying "from" relation, but the local payoff is stable: testimony is the exposure from which self-screening would have mattered. The particle compresses that danger into a short verbal complement instead of leaving concealment abstract.

topics.headline: testimony defines the hiding problem
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the missing concealment aimed specifically at bodily testimony, while not forcing a single English gloss for the particle.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses the following clause as the complement of the concealment verb; the semantic alternatives are useful only as local pressure, not as separate parses.

words.gloss_range: subordinate direct witnessing in which bodily presence becomes adverse testimony
words.root_gloss_range: presence, witnessing, and evidentiary testimony are locally active; external recruitment or causation is not selected
words.prose: {{ar:يَشْهَدَ}} ({{tr:yashhada}}) is grammatically dependent on the preceding subordinating particle, so the testimony is embedded inside the concealment problem. Yet the root makes that embedded event vivid: presence with deeds becomes evidentiary speech against the actor. Form I keeps the witness direct, and the singular verb opens with hearing before absorbing sights and skins into one witness sequence. The root echo with the testimony already shown in 41:20-21 lets the ayah explain retrospectively what has just happened; 36:65 provides a broader embodied-testimony parallel without replacing this local list.

topics.headline: testimony remains subordinate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees testimony as the danger contained within the concealment clause, not as a fresh independent assertion.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as subjunctive after the particle, and attachment evidence places the clause under the concealment verb.

topics.headline: bodily presence turns into proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the organs testify because they were present with the deeds, not because witnesses are imported from outside.
topics.reason: The direct Form I witness verb and the coordinated bodily subjects support presence becoming evidentiary speech.

topics.headline: singular verb opens expanding witness list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader watches one grammatical witness slot widen into a coordinated bodily sequence that echoes the testimony scene of 41:20-21.
topics.reason: The singular verb agrees first with the following hearing noun, while the supplied references to 41:20-21 and 36:65 are coherent parallels.

words.gloss_range: prepositional phrase marking testimony as adverse burden against the addressed group
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) turns witnessing into liability. The preposition places the testimony against or upon the accused before the first bodily witness is named, so accusation frames the list from the start. Across the boundary from 41:21, the pronoun shift keeps the same people under pressure while changing complaint into direct indictment.

topics.headline: testimony is against them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the witness list as prosecution against the owners, not as neutral reporting.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the phrase to the witness verb, and its placement before the first witness makes adverse liability the frame.

words.gloss_range: possessed hearing faculty as the first nominative witness and evidentiary archive
words.root_gloss_range: hearing, listening, receiving, and heeding are locally narrowed to auditory reception as witness-bearing faculty
words.prose: {{ar:سَمْعُكُمْ}} ({{tr:samʿukum}}) is the first named subject of testimony. The possessed faculty acts against its own owners: what was theirs becomes a witness over them. Because the word is a verbal noun or faculty form, hearing can feel like capacity, reception, and record at once. It opens the ordered body-list, then sight and skins widen the archive; 17:36 and 41:20 help the reader hear the move from accountable faculties to faculties actively testifying.

topics.headline: owned faculty testifies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the first witness is the accused person's own hearing, not an external observer.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the first subject of the witness verb, and the suffix keeps ownership attached to the accused.

topics.headline: hearing includes reception and heeding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear auditory testimony as reception and response, while keeping the local referent as the hearing faculty.
topics.reason: The broader root range is relevant, but the local grammar selects the possessed faculty as witness.

topics.headline: hearing launches the body archive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows an ordered witness expansion from hearing to sight to skin, with earlier accountability language now turned into active testimony.
topics.reason: The word is first in the coordinated witness list, and the supplied references to 17:36 and 41:20 support the accountability-to-testimony shift.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector that adds sight at equal witness rank
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) begins the first coordinated expansion of the witness list. It keeps sight at the same syntactic rank as hearing rather than making it a gloss or aside, so the clause widens without resetting. The witness sequence grows by addition under the same adverse testimony pressure.

topics.headline: sight added without subordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second faculty added as another witness slot under the same clause.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the next witness item with the first subject rather than starting a new clause.

words.gloss_range: repeated negative particle distributing the concealment denial to the sight witness
words.prose: {{ar:لَآ}} ({{tr:lā}}) does not create a separate denial; it distributes the already active non-concealment frame to the sight category. By repeating the negative marker, the ayah gives sight its own place in the witness list. The written length in this first nor-link also slows the transition, making the enumeration feel deliberate.

topics.headline: sight receives its own nor-marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears sight singled out as its own witness category inside the same denial frame.
topics.reason: The particle appears inside the coordinated witness phrase and marks the next category without changing the governing clause.

topics.headline: extended first nor-link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first transition in the list as audibly paced rather than rushed.
topics.reason: The surface form preserves the extended written negative marker before the sight noun.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural sights coordinated as witnesses, with vision and discernment pressure
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, observing, perception, and insight are locally narrowed to plural visual witness under the testimony clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَبْصَٰرُكُمْ}} ({{tr:abṣārukum}}) shares subject agency with hearing while remaining plural and possessed. The sight-root can carry both vision and discernment, so the witness is not merely a camera-like body part; it is visual perception turned against its owners. Its plural form multiplies sight-lines, and its middle position carries the list from auditory reception toward bodily surface. The familiar hearing/sight gift-pair (23:78) is reversed here into accountability, while 41:20 and 41:40 keep sight inside the surah's evidence-and-vision thread.

topics.headline: owned sights share witness agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the accused person's own plural sights acting as coordinated witnesses against them.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the word with the first witness subject, and the plural possessed form supports multiplied owned witness-lines.

topics.headline: sight includes perceptive awareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears visual testimony as perception and discernment while keeping the local referent as the plural sights.
topics.reason: The root range supports vision and insight, but local grammar narrows the word to a possessed plural faculty in the witness list.

topics.headline: gifted faculties become witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the familiar hearing/sight pair turned from divine gift or human perception into forensic evidence.
topics.reason: The supplied concrete references support the contrast with 23:78 and same-surah links to 41:20 and 41:40.

topics.headline: middle item carries the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the list move from hearing through sight toward skin while the repeated ownership suffix binds the witnesses together.
topics.reason: The word occupies the middle witness position and shares the repeated suffix cadence with the surrounding owned body terms.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector that carries the list from sensory pair to skins
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) gives skins equal coordinate rank while also escalating beyond the standard hearing-and-sight pair. The connector keeps the third witness inside the same clause, yet the sequence now moves from perception to bodily surface. Skins therefore arrive as a climax, not an appendix.

topics.headline: coordination escalates to skin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears skins added at equal rank while also feeling the witness list expand beyond perception.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the third witness with the prior subjects, and the order makes the addition an escalation to bodily surface.

words.gloss_range: repeated nor-marker giving skins an independent witness slot
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) repeats the distributed negative marker before skins. That repetition prevents the third witness from being swallowed by the earlier sensory pair: hearing is named, sight receives its own nor-link, and skins receive another. The result is a paced triad of witness categories.

topics.headline: skins singled out by repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears skins as a distinct witness category, not as a trailing afterthought.
topics.reason: The repeated particle sits before the third coordinate and completes the distributed witness enumeration.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural skins as coordinated subject-witnesses and bodily surfaces of disclosure
words.root_gloss_range: skin, hide, covering, and bodily surface are locally focused on the body's outer covering as a distributed witness surface
words.prose: {{ar:جُلُودُكُمْ}} ({{tr:julūdukum}}) completes the witness expansion by making the body's covering surface a subject of testimony. The word is not an object being described; it is coordinated with hearing as a witness, and the suffix makes the irony direct: their own skins bear against them. The root image reverses cover into disclosure, while the plural distributes testimony across embodied surfaces. After hearing and sight, skins bring the list to concrete contact, and the hard d/k contact in the word's close reinforces that bodily endpoint. Its recurrence from 41:20-21 turns the dramatic skin testimony there into the analyzed witness category here.

topics.headline: owned skins act as witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the accused person's own bodily surface functioning as an agent of testimony.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the skins with the first witness subject, and the possessive suffix keeps ownership on the accused.

topics.headline: cover becomes record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the reversal that the outer covering meant to conceal becomes the record that uncovers.
topics.reason: The skin/covering field and plural concrete noun support distributed bodily-surface testimony in this clause.

topics.headline: 41:20-21 skin testimony explained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same skins from 41:20-21 carried into the rebuke as the witness whose surprise is being diagnosed.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah links to the prior skin testimony, and the local word repeats the same witness category.

topics.headline: contact surface closes the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the list arrive at concrete contact and bodily surface, with sound texture reinforcing the hard witness endpoint.
topics.reason: The word follows hearing and sight, and the distribution rows mark the skin cluster as locally salient.

words.gloss_range: connector that attaches the adversative explanation to the witness-list rebuke
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the adversative correction attached to what came before. The next clause does not float away from the body-witness scene; it explains why the absence of concealment existed. At the boundary from the prior dialogue, the connector helps the discourse move from dramatic testimony into analytic indictment.

topics.headline: correction remains tied to witness scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the false-belief clause as the explanation of the prior denial, not as an unrelated theological aside.
topics.reason: The connector is prefixed to the adversative particle, linking correction to the preceding witness enumeration and boundary shift.

words.gloss_range: adversative correction replacing tactical explanation with false belief as the cause
words.prose: {{ar:لَٰكِن}} ({{tr:lākin}}) pivots from witness mechanics to the actual cause. It corrects the expected explanation that they simply failed to anticipate bodily witnesses; the reason was a governing supposition about divine knowledge. Because it is a discourse particle, its force lies in relation between clauses, not in derivational root semantics.

topics.headline: false belief replaces tactical failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes that the ayah explains non-concealment by false theology, not by poor concealment tactics.
topics.reason: The adversative particle introduces the thought verb that governs the proposition about Allah's knowledge.

topics.headline: discourse force rather than derivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the analysis focused on clause correction instead of hunting for lexical root pressure in a particle.
topics.reason: The word is tagged as a particle with no lexical root in the input alignment.

words.gloss_range: second-person perfect thought verb governing the explicit false proposition
words.root_gloss_range: supposition, conjecture, expectation, and confidence are locally focused on an operative misjudgment strong enough to govern conduct
words.prose: {{ar:ظَنَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ẓanantum}}) names the hidden cause. The verb governs the following content clause, so the ayah does not leave their error vague; it exposes the exact proposition they treated as operative. The root can range from conjecture to settled expectation, and here that expectation was strong enough to shape conduct. Its Form I keeps the judgment with the accused themselves. The same root is picked up in 41:23 as the assumption that ruins them, with later recurrences extending the expectation-collapse thread (41:48; 41:50). The proposition it governs ties Allah, knowledge, quantity, and deeds into one false model.

topics.headline: thought verb exposes the proposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rebuke diagnose a precise belief-content rather than a vague mistake.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following clause the content object of the thought verb.

topics.headline: supposition strong enough to govern conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the thought as an operative expectation behind behavior, while not overtranslating the root as absolute certainty.
topics.reason: The lexical range is broad, but the adversative explanation shows that the supposition governed their non-concealment.

topics.headline: 41:23 turns supposition into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this cognition verb become the next ayah's named object of judgment.
topics.reason: The supplied same-surah rows identify 41:23 as an immediate reprise and verdict on the same supposition.

topics.headline: false thought joins knowledge and deeds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the mental error as the hinge joining Allah, knowledge, quantity, and deeds.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and summary rows match the local clause, where the thought verb governs a proposition about Allah knowing much of what they do.

words.gloss_range: content particle embedding the false proposition under the thought verb
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) marks the boundary where psychology becomes proposition. It embeds the following clause under the preceding thought verb, protecting the ayah from sounding as though it asserts any limit to divine knowledge. The particle makes the false claim explicit and locates the error inside their thought content.

topics.headline: reported belief separated from truth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the reported false proposition from the ayah's own assertion.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the clause introduced here the content object of the thought verb, with the divine name governed as the embedded subject.

words.gloss_range: divine proper name as accusative embedded subject of the denied knowledge claim
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, devotion, awe, and disputed derivational background heighten the proper name, while the local word functions as the divine name
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:llāha}}) is the accusative subject inside the embedded false proposition. That makes the assumption theological and personal: they imagined a limit in Allah's knowing, not merely a gap in impersonal surveillance. The proper name blocks abstraction, and the surrounding worship/awe field heightens the audacity of the claim. The same name has just appeared in 41:21 as the One who made skins speak, so the prior divine agency directly answers the current denial of knowledge; 58:7 supplies a wider counter-formula of divine knowledge of secrecy.

topics.headline: Allah is the subject misjudged
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the false proposition targeting Allah's knowing directly, after the belief frame has been opened.
topics.reason: The divine name is governed by the content particle as the embedded subject of the knowledge verb.

topics.headline: proper name blocks abstract surveillance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the error as a claim about divine knowledge of deeds, not generic monitoring.
topics.reason: The local proposition pairs the proper divine name with the knowledge verb and deed-field.

topics.headline: awe field heightens audacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the audacity of denying knowledge to the named God while keeping the local function as a proper name.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute and worship/awe field can color the proper name, but local grammar does not turn it into a common noun.

topics.headline: 41:21 answers the denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the One who made skins speak in 41:21 as the very subject they imagined did not know much.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete links to 41:21 and 58:7, both reinforcing the contradiction between divine agency/knowledge and their assumption.

topics.headline: divine agency becomes indictment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader watches the discourse move from created speech explained by Allah to a prosecutorial diagnosis of what they assumed about Allah.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect prior divine agency to the current embedded proposition.

words.gloss_range: embedded negation of the knowledge predicate inside their reported belief
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is the hinge of the false proposition, not the ayah's own denial of divine knowledge. Because it sits inside the content clause governed by the thought verb, the syntax reports and exposes their negated model. The particle turns the misjudgment into a specific claim: Allah, they assumed, did not know much.

topics.headline: negation belongs to their belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids mistaking the embedded denial for the narrator's assertion.
topics.reason: The particle negates the knowledge verb inside the content clause under the thought verb.

topics.headline: negation specifies the false theology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the error sharpen from general misjudgment into a denial that Allah knew much of their deeds.
topics.reason: The negation is placed directly before the knowledge predicate within the embedded proposition.

words.gloss_range: embedded imperfect knowledge predicate falsely limited by a quantified object
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, awareness, certainty, and marks of knowledge are locally focused on divine knowing as the predicate they falsely negate
words.prose: {{ar:يَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:yaʿlamu}}) is the predicate inside the reported false claim. It takes the quantified object that follows, making the disputed issue not knowledge in the abstract but the imagined quantity of deeds known. The imperfect form gives their false claim standing force, as though divine knowing had an ongoing limit. At the same time, the broader knowledge field and parallels such as 67:14 sharpen the contradiction: bodily witnesses expose deeds, but Allah's knowledge is not dependent on witnesses. The same surah's divine-awareness thread also keeps this negated claim under pressure (41:12; 41:36; 41:47).

topics.headline: knowledge takes a quantity object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the false belief focused on how much of their deeds Allah knew, not on an undefined knowledge problem.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following quantity word as the object or quantified extent of the knowledge verb.

topics.headline: divine knowledge contrasted with testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that testimony makes deeds manifest against the accused, while divine knowledge was the thing falsely limited.
topics.reason: The local proposition places the knowledge root between Allah and the deed-field, while the witness list supplies the evidentiary contrast.

topics.headline: ongoing reported predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears their error as a standing claim within reported belief, not as the ayah endorsing a momentary event.
topics.reason: The imperfect is embedded under the content particle governed by the thought verb.

topics.headline: creation knowledge answers the assumption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can place the false limit beside Quranic claims that the Creator knows and beside this surah's divine-awareness thread.
topics.reason: The concrete references to 67:14 and the same-surah knowledge thread support contrast without overriding the embedded local syntax.

words.gloss_range: accusative substantive quantity marking the imagined 'much' outside divine knowledge
words.root_gloss_range: abundance, many-ness, increase, and multiplication are locally focused on the quantified extent falsely denied as known
words.prose: {{ar:كَثِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:kathīran}}) is the mathematical center of the false belief. As an accusative adjective used substantively or as quantified extent, it makes abundance itself the contested object: they did not deny all knowledge, but imagined much of their conduct outside it. Its position before the following partitive phrase foregrounds magnitude before the deed-source is named, and the nasal transition into the next word audibly binds quantity to the partitive field. The abundance echo with 102:1 and the same-surah quantity language of 41:4 sharpen the danger of measuring wrongly.

topics.headline: not total denial but much mismeasured
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the false belief as a selective mismeasurement of much, not as a simple claim that Allah knows nothing.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as an accusative object or quantified extent of the knowledge verb, specified by the following partitive phrase.

topics.headline: abundance becomes the focus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices quantity itself becoming the content of the denied knowledge.
topics.reason: The qualitative adjective functions substantively or adverbially in the local predicate.

topics.headline: magnitude before deed-source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears 'much' first, then learns from what domain that much is being selected.
topics.reason: The quantity precedes the partitive phrase, and the phonetic row supports the audible binding into the following word.

topics.headline: abundance as dangerous measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this mismeasured 'much' to Quranic and same-surah quantity language where abundance becomes spiritually dangerous.
topics.reason: The supplied references to 102:1 and 41:4 support a quantity/abundance contrast without changing the local accusative function.

words.gloss_range: contracted partitive phrase linking the quantified much to the open deed-domain
words.prose: {{ar:مِّمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) prevents the quantity from floating. The contraction fuses the partitive preposition with the relative element, so the imagined 'much' is selected from the open domain of what they do. It bridges the foregrounded magnitude to the final action verb and keeps both sides active: partition and whatever-deed field.

topics.headline: much selected from deeds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the false quantity tied to deeds as its source-set, not left as abstract abundance.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence connects the phrase to the quantity word and to the final relative/action clause.

topics.headline: source and domain compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how one contracted word tightens the relation between quantity and performed action.
topics.reason: The surface contraction carries both partitive source and relative-domain force in the local clause.

words.gloss_range: open-object Form I imperfect closing on broad ongoing performed conduct
words.root_gloss_range: deeds, work, practice, action, and produced effect are locally focused on the broad conduct-domain from which the false 'much' is selected
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿmalūn}}) closes the ayah on performed conduct. After the relative element in the preceding partitive contraction, the verb has no explicit direct object, so the field remains broad: deeds, practices, and produced effects. Form I keeps the action plain rather than specialized, and the imperfect second-person ending leaves the addressed group enclosed by ongoing conduct. Same-surah links such as 41:40 and the wider deed-accounting thread (41:20; 41:27; 41:33; 41:46) make the final word the place where the false knowledge gap tries to carve out space.

topics.headline: deeds left broad and traceable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final action-domain as broad performed conduct, not a narrow or named object.
topics.reason: The verb follows the relative element and lacks an explicit direct object, leaving the conduct-domain open.

topics.headline: plain doing, not specialized craft
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears ordinary performed action as the accountable field rather than a specialized derived action type.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form I, and the CRITICAL rows contrast this with more specialized derived meanings.

topics.headline: deeds answer the knowledge gap
topics.reader_payoff: The reader places the final deed-field inside the surah's network of action, seeing, testimony, and recompense.
topics.reason: The supplied references to 41:40 and nearby deed-accounting verses support the local close on performed action.

topics.headline: final ongoing address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah end with the accused still directly addressed and surrounded by their ongoing actions.
topics.reason: The final imperfect verb is second-person plural and stands in the ayah's closing position.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تستترون ... يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم sets attempted concealment against the subject's own bodily witnesses.
baseline_models.mechanism: The bodily envelope is double-use: hearing receives, sight observes, and skin covers the actor, yet these same sites can issue knowledgeable evidence against the possessive self.

activation_trace.role: Literal hiding and covering supply the privacy action that the verse denies as protection from testimony.
A knowledgeable declaration makes the body's testimony evidentiary disclosure rather than mere presence.
Auditory reception supplies an evidence-bearing channel located inside the actor's own sensorium.
The body's outer sheath supplies the apparent boundary of privacy and then becomes one of its witnesses.

changed_reading.before: The addressees merely failed to hide deeds from eventual witnesses.
changed_reading.after: Their own boundary and receptors form an internal archive: the apparatus used to inhabit private action is already capable of disclosing it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون explicitly joins supposition about divine knowledge to a large field of deeds.
baseline_models.mechanism: A low-certainty estimate about limited divine awareness becomes practical permission for numerous intentional acts; an epistemic error organizes conduct.

activation_trace.role: Uncertain conjecture supplies the weak epistemic basis on which the actors nevertheless rely.
Disclosure to a knower supplies the awareness whose scope their conjecture falsely restricts.
Numerical abundance makes the supposed blind zone broad rather than exceptional.
Deliberate action turns the faulty estimate into an operating rule for conduct.

changed_reading.before: They held an abstractly mistaken belief that God did not know some deeds.
changed_reading.after: They converted weak conjecture about the scope of divine awareness into behavioral permission for many deliberate acts; the failure is practical epistemology.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: سمعكم وأبصاركم وجلودكم are grammatically possessed by the accused yet stand against them.
baseline_models.mechanism: The acting self is distributed across perceptive and working members; those members bear signs that can make the self legible against its preferred account.

activation_trace.role: A condition-mark that bears witness makes bodily evidence readable as a sign of what occurred.
Inner discernment and self-witnessing turn sight from a passive organ into a mode of self-knowledge.
The working limb binds intentional deeds to the bodily members that execute and retain their trace.

changed_reading.before: The organs function as external witnesses unexpectedly attached to the accused.
changed_reading.after: The testimony is distributed self-evidence: the self's own perceptive and operative members contradict the unitary story it tells about itself.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah constructs a deliberate anti-reception system around heart, ear, and interpersonal space, then shows the supposedly disabled sensorium testifying. Concealment is therefore not only hiding deeds but managing what can enter, register, and count as knowledge.

activation_trace.role: Entry into a protective interior supplies a claimed heart-level enclosure that extends the focus's hiding inward.
Literal weight in the ear turns hearing from an open receiver into a deliberately burdened channel.
An obstructing screen formalizes separation between message and hearer as part of the concealment architecture.
Gentle direction toward truth supplies the available perceptual route against which blindness is chosen.
Intentional choosing supplies agency to blindness, making sensory failure a preference rather than a mere deficit.
Refusal of understanding and compliance makes non-listening an organized stance toward the recitation.
Mixed vocal noise supplies the masking technique used to prevent meaningful reception.
Coercive victory supplies the intended payoff of sensory masking, exposing it as strategy.

structural_cues: 41:5 stacks heart-coverings, ear-weight, and a between-space barrier before the reciprocal challenge to work.
41:17 calls blindness preferred over guidance; 41:26 coordinates non-listening and noise as a bid to prevail; 41:44 repeats ear-weight and blindness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies layered barriers, chosen blindness, and coordinated masking noise; I infer that these are practical forms of تستترون whose reversal is organ testimony. A live alternative is that the passages diagnose rejection of revelation without specifying how the later organs retained evidence.

changed_reading.before: Their bodies simply defeat an attempt to hide private misconduct.
changed_reading.after: The witnessing body reverses a cultivated anti-reception system: faculties they burdened, blinded, and masked still register enough to disclose the conduct that system enabled.

context_deltas.mechanism: Heaven and earth first answer divine address; immediately before the focus the organs testify, and the skins explain that the creator made every thing speak. Bodily evidence belongs to a creation-to-return arc of responsive matter.

activation_trace.role: Created heaven and earth's willing compliance supplies an earlier model of matter answering divine address.
The prior scene supplies the actual knowledgeable declaration that the focus retrospectively explains.
The bodily sheath becomes a speaking respondent, joining material boundary to accountable voice.
Articulate speech supplies the explicit enabling event and generalizes it from skins to every thing.
Creative origination grounds bodily speech in the same agency that constituted the speakers.
Return restores the created body to the forum where its latent responsiveness becomes testimony.

structural_cues: 41:11 gives heaven and earth a spoken obedient answer; 41:20 enacts testimony; 41:21 gives skins an answer and attributes speech to every thing.
41:21 closes with creation, first occurrence, and return, placing bodily speech inside a full temporal arc.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel scenes of created entities answering and an explicit creator-enabled speech claim; I infer a shared mechanism of created responsiveness. The materially live alternative is a one-time forensic miracle rather than a standing capacity of matter.

changed_reading.before: The organs are unexpectedly animated at judgment to furnish evidence.
changed_reading.after: Their testimony culminates a surah-wide responsiveness of creation: the body was never inert property under the actor's exclusive control and answers its creator upon return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's conjecture is named as the cause of ruin, then situated amid attached companions who beautify the accessible temporal field until liability becomes fixed. The false estimate is sustained by a social-perceptual environment.

activation_trace.role: Repeated weak conjecture identifies the focus's estimate itself as the immediately named causal object.
A fall into destruction supplies the consequence assigned directly to that conjecture.
An attached companion supplies the social carrier that can stabilize a shared field of judgment.
Making something appear good supplies the perceptual editing by which the visible field becomes persuasive.
Fixed and deserved liability supplies the endpoint at which curated conjecture hardens into consequence.

structural_cues: 41:23 makes ذلكم ظنكم the subject of أرداكم, giving the conjecture explicit causal force.
41:25 places paired companions, beautification of what is before and behind, and fixed judgment in one sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies direct ruin by conjecture and a later companion-beautification sequence; I infer that social curation helps sustain the focus's false estimate. The alternative is that the beautification concerns deeds and temporal expectations broadly, not this specific belief about divine knowledge.

changed_reading.before: The actors independently make a mistaken estimate about what God knows.
changed_reading.after: Their estimate is an actionable, socially scaffolded enclosure: companions beautify the available field until weak conjecture feels inhabitable and its resulting liability becomes fixed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah mirrors the focus's human faculties with divine hearing and knowing, then denies hiddenness, predicates discerning sight of deeds, and closes with total cognitive enclosure. Organ testimony publicizes evidence but does not fill a gap in divine awareness.

activation_trace.role: Hearing predicated of God supplies a divine-side receptive term that mirrors the focus's human hearing without equating them.
Full disclosure to the knower directly opposes the focus's conjecture of limited awareness.
Hiddenness and covering are explicitly negated at the divine vantage, collapsing the proposed blind zone.
Deliberate work is first licensed rhetorically and then made the direct object of discerning observation.
Penetrating discernment supplies sight as comprehensive awareness of deeds rather than limited ocular capture.
Complete cognitive enclosure supplies the terminal spatial model in which no deed can sit outside awareness.

structural_cues: 41:36 pairs السميع with العليم; 41:40 pairs لا يخفون علينا with بما تعملون بصير.
41:54 closes the surah by placing every thing within divine encompassing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored faculty terms, explicit non-hiddenness, discernment of deeds, and encompassing; I infer that bodily witnesses manifest knowledge rather than produce it. The alternative is that their primary function is public forensic proof despite prior divine knowledge.

changed_reading.before: The organs provide information that exposes deeds otherwise left unobserved.
changed_reading.after: No evidentiary gap ever existed: embodied testimony makes already encompassed knowledge public and self-involving, so concealment fails at the level of ontology before it fails in court.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later deeds accrue for or against the self, while signs shown within selves disclose truth under universal witness. The focus's عليهم can therefore be read as action returning through embodied self-evidence, not merely alien accusation.

activation_trace.role: Intentional action supplies the deed whose effect is syntactically returned to its doer.
The very self or identity supplies the beneficiary and bearer of its own action.
Signs located in their own selves make the body an internal evidentiary field.
Emergence into clarity supplies the disclosure process by which inward signs become decisive.
Reality matching what is the case supplies the truth disclosed by signs within the self.
Universal knowledgeable witness situates embodied self-disclosure inside a complete evidentiary frame.

structural_cues: 41:46 balances عمل صالح فلنفسه against أساء فعليها, returning action to the self.
41:53 moves from signs in horizons and selves to disclosure of truth and universal witness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies action returning to the self and signs disclosed within selves; I infer that organ testimony is one concrete mode of this self-return. The alternative is that أنفسهم denotes human interiority generally and is not specifically linked to the named organs.

changed_reading.before: Body parts side with an external prosecution against their owner.
changed_reading.after: The body is where action returns to and becomes legible within the self; testimony against them is the self's own enacted structure disclosing truth.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a lexicalized, branch-distant hearing-looking pattern rather than the ordinary sense of سمع. It remains anchored by the focus's exact progression from hearing and sights to supposition and work. Downstream prose should present it only as a diagnostic analogy for epistemic habit, not as the lexical meaning of سمعكم.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ... ولكن ظننتم ... مما تعملون places hearing, seeing, conjecture, and action in one focus sequence.

activation_trace.role: A hearing-looking pattern that fails to see clearly and then acts by conjecture unexpectedly binds the focus's sensory terms to its epistemic error.
Ordinary ocular inspection supplies the perceptual check that the activated pattern fails to complete.
Weak conjecture supplies the substitute conclusion adopted when sensory apprehension does not mature into knowledge.
Intentional action supplies the behavioral endpoint of the failed sensory-to-knowledge sequence.

changed_reading.before: Hearing and sight only record deeds and later report them.
changed_reading.after: The same faculties may also expose a pre-deed habit: sampling sound and sight without attaining insight, then allowing supposition to govern action.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain material analogy from fruit sheaths and gestation to skin and concealed deeds. It remains anchored in تستترون, جلودكم, and لا يعلم, while 41:47 explicitly surrounds emergence from coverings and hidden bearing with knowledge. Downstream prose should label it an exploratory mechanism, not claim that the ayah lexically identifies skin with a plant sheath or pregnancy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins covering, bodily skin, supposedly limited knowledge, and deeds held within embodied life.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the attempted static occlusion whose material behavior the later emergence sequence revises.
The body's outer sheath supplies the focus-side container from which evidence can be imagined as emerging.
Awareness supplies the disputed relation between a hidden interior and the knower.
Knowledge explicitly encloses both outward emergence and inward bearing, defeating opacity at either stage.
Bringing something out of hiddenness supplies the directional transition from containment to disclosure.
A plant's enclosing vessel supplies the material analogue for a cover that contains rather than erases what is inside.
Hidden inward bearing supplies a second containment process already fully within knowledge.
Release by birth supplies the second outward transition, reinforcing disclosure from an enclosed interior.

changed_reading.before: Skin and concealment form a static screen intended to keep deeds unseen.
changed_reading.after: Embodied cover can be imagined as a containing sheath: it preserves what is within until hidden content emerges as evidence, all while already enclosed by knowledge.

strongest_changes: Failed hiding becomes the reversal of a surah-wide program of sensory insulation: covered hearts, weighted ears, chosen blindness, and organized noise.
Organ testimony belongs to a creation-wide pattern of answering and creator-enabled speech rather than an arbitrary late animation.
Divine hearing and knowing, discerning sight of deeds, and total encompassing remove any evidentiary gap; bodily testimony is self-involving disclosure within prior complete knowledge.
The destructive conjecture is not merely private error but can be carried by companions and a beautified perceptual field.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet made the focus a hinge between anti-reception and disclosure: the same senses that were strategically disabled become witnesses, while the unusual sensory-guesswork branch and the later sheath-emergence sequence preserved two contained readings a conservative synthesis could miss.
remaining_uncertainties: The construction ما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد can foreground inability to hide from the organs or denial that fear of their testimony motivated concealment; both support failed privacy but distribute agency differently.
The link from companion-driven beautification in 41:25 to the specific conjecture about divine knowledge is abductive; the packet also permits a broader link to deeds and temporal expectations.
The sheath and gestation model is materially coherent but cross-domain and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Concealment fails because the witnesses are internal.** **س ت ر B001** gives covering and concealment; the same witness roots from 41:20 recur inside the attempted privacy. The grammar says they were not hiding from the organs themselves. I infer that their model of secrecy assumed observation comes only from outside. The ayah reads as a correction of spatial epistemology: the archive is coextensive with the actor.
2. **Uncertain supposition displaces clear knowledge.** **ظ ن ن B003** gives uncertain supposition, while **ع ل م B001** gives knowledge as something becomes clear. Their supposition concerns the scope of divine knowledge and licenses **ع م ل B001**. I infer a causal arrow from a narrowed theology of knowledge to conduct. The failure is not only a wrong proposition but a privacy mechanism built from it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:40 states that those who incline away in the signs are not hidden, and closes with divine sight of their work. 41:53–54 finally surrounds horizons, selves, and all things with witnessing and encompassing knowledge.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Concealment failed because the body was inside the hiding place.** Lexically, `س ت ر B001` is covering/concealment, `ش ه د B002` knowledge-bearing testimony, and `ظ ن ن B003` uncertain supposition. Structurally, the same three bodily witnesses from 41:20 are repeated under the negated `تستترون`, then the actual concealment strategy is traced to a supposition about divine knowledge. I assign concealment the role of managing external visibility and the organs the role of observers that cannot be placed outside one’s acts. The inferred arrow is that a false epistemic model makes concealment appear effective. The ayah reads as a design failure in secrecy: the supposed cover contains its own witnesses.

2. **A supposition becomes a behavioral permission.** `ع ل م B001` is knowing as a thing becomes clear, opposed here by “does not know much,” while `ع م ل B001` is intentional conduct. The knowledge claim precedes the scope of action it allegedly excludes. I infer that minimizing what is known lowers the actor’s perceived cost of acting. The reading changes from an abstract theological error to a causal premise underwriting conduct.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:23 explicitly named the supposition as the cause of ruin, confirming the behavioral-permission reading. 41:26’s organized command not to listen showed the same epistemic model scaling from private concealment into collective channel control.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin üstünü veya önünü kapatarak onu görünmez kılma eylemidir.
Örtme işini sağlayan örtü, perde veya engeli de adlandırır.
Kişinin bir örtü ya da engelin ardında görünmez olması anlamına da uzanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme eyleminde, örtünmeye yarayan nesnelerde ve örtü ardında gizlenme sonucunda birleşir. Nesne türleri değişse de ortak çekirdek, görüşü kapatma ve görünmez kılmadır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Fiziksel kapatma eylemi, bunu sağlayan örtü veya engel ve kişinin böylece görünmez olması birlikte kastedildiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Eylemi, örtü ya da engel aracını ve gizlenme sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin bir nesneyi fiziksel olarak kapattığı geçişli eylem bağlamlarında doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir nesneyi kapatarak görünmez kılma eylemini korur.
error_profile.loses: Örtü veya engel adını ve kişinin kendisinin gizlenmesi anlamını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin örtü ya da engel arkasına geçerek görünmez olduğu bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin görünmez duruma geçmesi sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir nesneyi örtme eylemini ve örtü ya da engel adını dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir şeyi örtmek ve görünmez kılmak
arkasına saklanılan örtü ya da engel
güneşi veya başka bir şeyi kesen perde

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Fiziksel örtü, perde veya engel adı ile kişinin bunların ardında gizlenmesi bu dalda belirgindir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bilgiyi saklama, gizlilik ve açıklığın karşıtı olma komşu dalın ayrıca kapsadığı alanlardır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyi görünür veya bilinir olmaktan çıkarma düşüncesinde kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın çekirdeği fiziksel olarak örtme ve örtü ardında gizlenmedir; komşu dal ise fiziksel görünmezliğin yanında bilgiyi saklama ve gizlilik alanına açıkça yayılır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kişinin bir engelin ardına geçip gizlenmesi ve perde türü nesneler bu dalın ek kapsamıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir şeyin üzerine ya da önüne örtü getirerek onu kapatma eylemini ve örtüyü kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal kapak veya örtü koyma çekirdeğinde kalırken bu dal, örtü arkasında gizlenme sonucunu da açık bir anlam parçası olarak içerir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; en güçlü sınır karşılaştırmaları fiziksel örtmeyle gizli tutma arasındaki ayrım ve salt kapatma ile kişinin gizlenmesi arasındaki kapsam farkıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi utanma ve çekingenlik duygusunu, cinsel davranışta kendini sakınmayı ve bu niteliklerle betimlenen kişileri açıkça birlikte verir. Dalın ahlaki ve davranışsal çerçevesi bu kanıtı doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, fiziksel örtmeyi değil, kişinin utanma duygusunu, çekingenliğini ve cinsel davranışta kendini sakınmasını anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel utanma ve kendini sakınma anlamları ile kişileri betimleyen biçimler ayrılır; kalıba bağlı ifadeler bütün dalın çıplak anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kişinin utanma duygusuyla ölçülü ve çekingen davranması, özellikle cinsel ilişkilerde kendini uygun olmayandan sakınması ve bu niteliklerle tanımlanması.

facets.statement: Utanma duygusuna sahip olma ve bu duyguyla çekingen davranmadır.
Cinsel ilişkilerde uygun olmayandan kendini sakınma ve davranış temizliğini korumadır.
Bu nitelikleri taşıyan kadın veya erkeği betimleyen kullanımları vardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar utanma, çekingenlik ve cinsel davranışta kendini sakınma alanlarını aynı dalda toplar. Kişi betimlemeleri bu niteliklerin taşıyıcısını gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem çekingen ve ölçülü davranma duygusu hem de cinsel ilişkilerde kendini sakınma boyutu birlikte anlatıldığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Utanma duygusunu, davranışsal çekingenliği ve cinsel alandaki kendini sakınmayı birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Duygu ve çekingen davranışın öne çıktığı, cinsel ölçülülüğün ayrıca belirtilmediği bağlamlarda doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Utanma duygusunu ve çekingen davranma yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Cinsel ilişkilerde kendini sakınma ve bu nitelikle kişi betimleme boyutunu dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin cinsel ilişkilerde uygun olmayandan kendini sakınmasının öne çıktığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Cinsel davranışta kendini sakınma yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel utanma duygusunu ve çekingen davranış kapsamını dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: onda ne utanma duygusu ne de akıl var

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Cinsel ilişkilerde kendini sakınma ve bu nitelikle kadın ya da erkeği betimleme bu dalda açıkça bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Utanma duygusunun kişiyi durdurması ve ona sürekli bağlı kalması komşu dalda özellikle öne çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da utanma duygusunun kişide bulunmasını ve davranışı sınırlamasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal utanma duygusunu cinsel ölçülülük ve kişi nitelemeleriyle birlikte verir; komşu dal ise utanmanın kişiyi alıkoyan ve sürdürülen bir tutum olması üzerinde yoğunlaşır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Genel utanma duygusu ve çekingenlik bu dalın cinsel alan dışına taşan bölümüdür.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Cinsel organın veya kadının yasak ilişkiden ve kuşkudan korunması komşu dalın daha belirgin sınırıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da cinsel ilişkilerde uygun olmayandan uzak durma ve davranış temizliğini koruma alanında kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın kapsamı utanma ve çekingenliği de içerir; komşu dal ise cinsel korunmuşluk ve yasak ilişkiden uzak durma çekirdeğine daha sıkı bağlıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü değerlendirildi; utanmanın davranışı sınırlaması ve cinsel korunmuşluk, bu dalın iki ana sınırını en açık biçimde karşılaştıran komşulardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tekil biçimi bir yer adı ve iki dağdan birinin adı olarak, ikil biçimi ise iki vadinin adı olarak verir. Geçici çerçevenin iki dağın da aynı adı taşıdığı yönündeki izlenimi desteklenmediğinden dal bu ayrımı koruyacak biçimde yeniden kurulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yalnız belirli coğrafi varlıkların özel adlarını kapsar; ortak tür adı, fiziksel örtme veya iki dağın aynı adı taşıdığı iddiasını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam belirli tekil ve ikil ad biçimlerine bağlıdır; buradan genel bir yer, dağ veya vadi anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Tekil biçimi belirli bir yerin ve ayrıca iki dağdan birinin özel adı, ikil biçimi ise belirli iki vadinin ortak özel adıdır.

facets.statement: Tekil biçim belirli bir coğrafi yerin özel adı olarak kullanılır.
Aynı tekil biçim, birlikte anılan iki dağdan birinin özel adıdır.
İkil biçim, belirli iki vadinin ortak özel adı olarak kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt tekil ve ikil biçimlerin farklı coğrafi gönderimleri olduğunu gösterir. Tekil biçim bir yer veya bir dağ, ikil biçim ise iki vadi için kullanılan özel addır.

concept_gloss.text: bir yer ya da dağ adı ile iki vadinin adı
concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız kanıtta belirtilen tekil yer veya dağ adı ile ikil vadi adı gönderimlerini birlikte özetlemek için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Tekil biçimin yer veya dağ, ikil biçimin iki vadi adı olmasını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir yerin ya da bir dağın özel adı

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal kendi kanıtında belirtilen bir yer veya dağ ile iki vadiye gönderme yapar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal başka ad biçimleriyle anılan bir dağ veya iki tepeye gönderme yapar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da dağ veya başka coğrafi varlıklar için kullanılan özel adları içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ortaklık yalnız yer adı alanındadır; dalların ad biçimleri ve gösterdikleri coğrafi varlıklar birbirinden bağımsızdır, bu nedenle anlamdaşlık yoktur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü bağımsız coğrafi özel adlar bakımından incelendi; yalnız alan ortaklığı bulunduğundan temsil edici tek bir karşılaştırma yayımlandı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Bu dal packet düzeyinde inceleme statüsünde tutulmuş sınır-riskli malzemeyi taşır. Kanıt, tek bir yalın kök imgesinden çok biçime veya özel kullanıma bağlı dağınık adlandırmaları gösterdiği için dal yapısal bölme şartı koşmadan sınırlı bir adlandırma kümesi olarak okunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dalın öğeleri genel kök anlamı gibi genişletilmemeli, birbirinin yerine geçebilen tek bir sözlük karşılığı sayılmamalı ve yalnız kanıtta verilen biçim veya bağlam sınırı içinde tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kapsam verilen biçim veya özel kullanım sınırıyla bağlıdır; ortak bir yalın anlam ya da üretken genel kullanım varsayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kanıt, bir yanda dört sayısının özel adını, öte yanda dört buçuk temel ağırlık birimine eşit ve başka dilden alınmış bir ölçü adını tanıklar; bunlar tek kavram değil, ayrılması gereken iki ayrı anlamdır.

facets.statement: Bir kullanımda söz konusu biçim dört sayısını adlandırır.
Başka bir kullanımda dört buçuk temel ağırlık birimine eşit özel bir ölçüyü adlandırır.
Özel ağırlık adının başka bir dilden alındığı ayrıca belirtilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: İnceleme statüsündeki kanıt, tek bir birleşik anlamdan çok biçime veya özel bağlama bağlı sınırlı adlandırmaları gösterir; dal bu kayıtları kontrollü biçimde görünür tutar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bu karşılık, kanıttaki dağınık veya biçime bağlı adlandırma kümesini güvenli biçimde etiketler; tek ve birleşik bir sözlük anlamı değildir.

error_profile.preserves: Dalın inceleme statüsündeki sınırlı adlandırma niteliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Tek tek kullanımların özel göndergelerini kavram karşılığının içine ayrı ayrı taşımaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Biçimin doğrudan dört sayısını adlandırdığı sayma bağlamında kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Dört sayısını gösteren kullanımın sayısal değerini korur.
error_profile.loses: Dört buçuk temel ağırlık birimine eşit özel ölçü adını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Biçimin belirli bir ağırlık ölçüsünü adlandırdığı tartı bağlamında açıklayıcı karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Ölçünün dört buçuk temel ağırlık birimine eşit olmasını korur.
error_profile.loses: Dört sayısını adlandıran ayrı kullanımı ve ölçü adının köken bilgisini dışarıda bırakır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Dal yalnız sınırlı veya biçime bağlı adlandırma malzemesini tuttuğu için yayımlanacak güvenilir komşu ayrımı seçilmedi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli bir söz kalıbında bir kişinin iki taraf arasında elçi ve aracı olmasını açıkça tanımlar. Geçici dal çerçevesi bu görev ilişkisini doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız iki kişi arasındaki elçilik ve aracılık görevini bildiren belirli kalıba bağlıdır; genel örtme veya genel aracılık anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız sağlanan söz kalıbına bağlı aracılık anlamını verir; bu kullanım bağımsız ve genel bir kök anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli bir söz kalıbında, bir kişinin iki kişi arasında haber ve görüş taşıyan elçi ve aracı görevinde bulunması.

facets.statement: Bir kişi, iki kişi arasında elçi ve aracı olarak görev yapar.
Anlam yalnız kaynakta verilen iki taraflı söz kalıbı içinde tanıklanmıştır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, anlamı iki kişi arasındaki elçilik ve aracılık görevini bildiren belirli bir söz kalıbıyla sınırlar; bağımsız bir genel ad anlamı kurmaz.

source_details.summary: İki kişi arasındaki elçi ve aracı anlamındaki bu kalıplaşmış kullanım yalnız tek sözlükte tanıklanmıştır.

concept_gloss.text: iki kişi arasında elçilik yapan aracı
concept_gloss.applicability: Belirli söz kalıbında bir kişinin iki taraf arasında elçi ve aracı görevinde bulunduğu durum için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İki tarafı, aradaki kişiyi ve bu kişinin elçilik ile aracılık görevini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Elçilik ayrıntısının bağlamdan anlaşıldığı ve kişinin iki tarafı birbirine bağladığı cümlelerde doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir kişinin iki taraf arasında bağlantı kurması görevini korur.
error_profile.adds: Kaynakta verilen belirli kalıp ve elçilik görevi dışında kalan genel aracılık durumlarını da kapsayabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da tarafların arasına girerek iletişim veya anlaşma sağlamaya çalışan kişiyi ya da işi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal belirli bir söz kalıbında iki kişi arasındaki elçiyi adlandırır; komşu dal ise belirli kalıba ve elçilik görevine bağlı olmayan genel aracılığı kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İki kişi arasında konumlanan aracının ilişkisel yeri ve sabit söz kalıbı bu dalın sınırıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Vekillik, haber götürme ve güvence verme görevleri komşu dalın ayrıca içerdiği işlevlerdir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da başkaları adına bağlantı kuran veya haber taşıyan bir kişiyi içerebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda kişi iki belirli tarafın arasındaki aracı konumundadır; komşu dalda ise temsil, haber götürme veya güvence verme görevleri daha bağımsız biçimde öne çıkar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı hazır bulunma, bu hazır bulunuşa eşlik eden doğrudan görme ve bundan türeyen bulunma yeri kullanımlarıyla kuruyor. Eşin hazır olması ve ibadet yerleri gibi örnekler çekirdek anlamı genişletir; sözlü tanıklık veya bal anlamı bu dalın sınırına girmez.
